Choosing a PRIO-GRID conversion workflow

Source: vignettes/conversion-workflows.Rmd
conversion-workflows.Rmd

priogridR provides one conversion function for each common source-data format. All converters use a priogrid::pg_config() object as the source of truth for the target grid and temporal resolution.

Choose a converter

Source data Function Typical task
Point events or coordinate columns pg_from_points() Count events or summarize their values by cell and period
Raster layers pg_from_raster() Align continuous or categorical raster values to PRIO-GRID
Point, line, or polygon geometry pg_from_vector() Calculate counts, lengths, areas, coverage, or weighted values
NetCDF variables pg_from_netcdf() Select variables and layers before raster conversion
Values indexed by geographic units pg_from_table() Join a table to polygons and transfer the values to cells

The detailed guides are available through:

vignette("pg_from_points", package = "priogridR")
vignette("pg_from_raster", package = "priogridR")
vignette("pg_from_vector", package = "priogridR")
vignette("pg_from_netcdf", package = "priogridR")
vignette("pg_from_table", package = "priogridR")

A shared configuration

A small configuration is useful for examples and exploratory work:

config <- priogrid::pg_config(
  nrow = 18,
  ncol = 36,
  temporal_resolution = "1 year",
  start_date = as.Date("2020-12-31"),
  end_date = as.Date("2022-12-31"),
  verbose = FALSE
)

Use the default priogrid::pg_current_config() when the official global half-degree grid is required.

Common return types

Every converter accepts a return argument:

  • return = "data" returns a cell-level data frame;
  • return = "raster" returns a terra::SpatRaster; and
  • return = "result" returns a pg_result containing data, raster, and conversion metadata.

The default is "data". Use pg_write_result() to save tabular or raster outputs, or pass filename directly to a converter.

General advice

Check the coordinate reference system before conversion, distinguish missing values from meaningful zeros, and choose an aggregation rule that matches the meaning of the source variable. In particular, totals generally require a different transfer rule from rates, proportions, or categories.
